CONSTRUCT VALIDITY THREAT (C2 orthogonality): Header-only Jaccard is computed between valid vs expired requests WITH SAME body_variant. In the Flask implementation, preserved headers (Cache-Control, Set-Cookie, Vary) are determined SOLELY by body_variant (lines 92-100, 125-140 in run_experiment.py), NOT by auth state. Therefore valid and expired requests for the same body_variant produce IDENTICAL filtered headers → Jaccard=1.0 constant → Pearson r=0 trivially (correlation with constant is undefined/0). This does not validate that header-only Jaccard is a structural measure orthogonal to behavioral drift; it validates that in this implementation, drift does not affect the preserved headers. The test design conflates 'drift independence' with 'header invariance to drift by construction'.

CONSTRUCT VALIDITY THREAT (C4 full-vector): Header-varying probes (80 pairs) are created by manually mutating response headers (Cache-Control, Set-Cookie, Vary) AFTER receiving the response, while keeping body identical. This tests whether the fingerprint CAN detect header differences when they exist, not whether auth state naturally produces header differences. Body-varying probes (A vs C) achieve body-only=1.0 (bodies differ) and full=1.0; header-varying probes achieve body-only=0.0 and full=1.0. The full > body margin (0.38) comes entirely from synthetic header manipulation. Null probes (A vs A) correctly give full=0.0, body=0.0, status=0.0.
